content.title: About
content.content: Pre‑gelatinized organic millet flour is a whole‑grain product made from whole millet kernels that have undergone a pre‑gelatinization process, improving its solubility in cold liquids. The flour is certified organic, non‑GMO, and suitable for vegans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Millet is one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown for over 5,000 years in Africa and Asia.
Pre‑gelatinized flour quickly forms a gel, making it popular in gluten‑free recipes.
Organic millet is grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers.
The flour has a light yellow color and a mild nutty aroma.
Millet is drought‑tolerant, putting less pressure on water resources.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Millet flour provides slowly digestible carbs that help maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Millet contains magnesium, phosphorus, iron, and zinc, important for bones, energy, and immunity.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The flour is virtually fat‑free, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Ideal for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to millet.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or fermenting helps if consumed in large amounts.

items.title: Quality control
items.content: Improper storage can lead to mold growth and loss of nutritional quality.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add pre‑gelatinized millet flour to smoothies, porridges, gluten‑free breads, pancakes, and muffins. Its pre‑gelatinization allows it to thicken cold liquids quickly, perfect for sauces and dressings. It can replace wheat flour 1:1 in most recipes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer. Discard if you notice mold odor or discoloration.
